name: Methi Chicken

ingredients.name: Chicken thigh, boneless, skinless
ingredients.householdMeasure: about 3 medium thighs, cut in 3 cm pieces

equipment: Kadai or heavy-bottomed pan (about 18–20 cm) with a lid
Chopping board and a sharp knife
Small bowl and fork or whisk for the curd
Measuring spoons and a small kitchen scale (spoon measures are given for the scale-less)
Clean kitchen towel or paper towels to dry the leaves (salad spinner if you have one)

steps.title: Cut the chicken
steps.text: Cut 150 g boneless thigh into 3 cm pieces and pat them dry with paper towel.
steps.tip: Wash your hands, knife and board with hot soapy water after touching raw chicken.
steps.visualCue: Even pink-beige pieces, about the size of a large grape cluster, with no wet shine on the surface
steps.cameraCheck: The chicken pieces on the board
steps.videoShot: A knife cutting thigh meat into cubes.
steps.watchOut: Pieces of very different sizes, where small ones overcook and go dry while big ones stay raw in the middle; trim to even sizes.

steps.title: Pick the leaves
steps.text: Pull the leaves off the stems from about 100 g of fresh methi until you have 50 g of leaves in a bowl.
steps.visualCue: A bowl of loose small green leaves; the thin stems stay in your other hand
steps.videoShot: Fingers stripping leaves down a stem.
steps.watchOut: Leaving thick stems in, which taste more bitter and stay tough (sources say to use leaves only); if some stem comes along, pick it out before step 4.

steps.title: Wash and dry the leaves
steps.text: Rinse the leaves in a bowl of water twice, then spread them on a kitchen towel and pat them dry.
steps.visualCue: Water in the bowl runs clear on the second rinse; leaves look dry with no drops on them
steps.videoShot: Leaves being rinsed, then patted dry.
steps.watchOut: Wet leaves going into the pan, which thin the gravy and mute the flavour (a blog tip); keep patting until the towel stays dry.

steps.title: Chop the leaves
steps.text: Chop the dry leaves roughly into pieces about 1 cm wide.
steps.tip: Smell and nibble one leaf first. A little bitterness is normal; if it is very harsh, use only 30 g or add the kasuri methi alternative (see section 1).
steps.visualCue: A loose green pile, with a strong grassy-bitter smell
steps.videoShot: A knife rocking over a pile of leaves.
steps.watchOut: Chopping them very fine, which turns them into a paste that makes the curry bitter all through; a rough chop is enough.

steps.title: Slice the onion
steps.text: Slice 70 g (½ medium) onion into thin half-moons.
steps.visualCue: Thin even slices, about 3 mm thick
steps.videoShot: A knife slicing onion into half-moons.
steps.watchOut: Thick and thin slices mixed together, where the thin ones burn before the thick ones soften; slice evenly.

steps.title: Chop the tomato
steps.text: Chop 60 g (½ medium) tomato into small pieces.
steps.visualCue: Small red pieces with the juice kept on the board or in the bowl
steps.videoShot: A tomato being diced.
steps.watchOut: Throwing away the juice, which the gravy needs; scrape it all into the bowl.

steps.title: Mince the ginger and garlic
steps.text: Mince 1 cm ginger (5 g) and 2 garlic cloves (6 g) fine.
steps.visualCue: A small pile of wet, pale-yellow bits with a sharp smell
steps.videoShot: Garlic crushed under a knife and chopped.
steps.watchOut: Big chunks of garlic, which burn black and taste bitter in the pan; mince it fine.

steps.title: Slit the chilli
steps.text: Cut 1 green chilli (4 g) lengthways, leaving it joined at the stem.
steps.visualCue: A chilli with one clean cut down its length and the seeds just showing
steps.videoShot: A knife slitting a green chilli.
steps.watchOut: Touching your eyes after handling chilli, which burns; wash your hands with soap straight after.

steps.title: Whisk the curd
steps.text: Put 40 g (3 tbsp) curd in a small bowl and whisk with a fork until smooth.
steps.visualCue: A smooth, pourable cream with no lumps
steps.videoShot: A fork whisking curd in a bowl.
steps.watchOut: Lumpy cold curd going straight into hot masala, where it splits into grains; whisk smooth and let it sit out of the fridge while you cook.

steps.title: Mix the powders
steps.text: In a small bowl put ¼ tsp (0.5 g) turmeric, ¾ tsp (2 g) Kashmiri chilli powder and 1 tsp (3 g) coriander powder.
steps.visualCue: Three colours of powder (yellow, red, brown) side by side in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Spoons of powder tapped into a bowl.
steps.watchOut: Adding the powders dry to a very hot pan, where they burn in seconds and taste bitter; keep the bowl next to the stove and add it in step 16 with water.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Put the kadai on medium heat and add 1 tbsp (12 g) oil.
steps.visualCue: The oil looks thin and shimmers, and a cumin seed dropped in fizzes at once
steps.videoShot: Oil swirled in a hot pan.
steps.watchOut: Smoking oil, which means it is too hot and will burn the spices; lower the heat for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Temper the cumin and bay leaf
steps.text: Add ½ tsp (1 g) cumin seeds and 1 bay leaf.
steps.visualCue: Cumin seeds sizzle, turn a shade darker and smell nutty within 10–15 seconds
steps.videoShot: Seeds crackling in hot oil.
steps.watchOut: Cumin turning dark brown and smelling acrid, which means it burned; if so, wipe the pan and start again with fresh oil.

steps.title: Brown the onion
steps.text: Add the sliced onion and 2 pinches of salt from your 2.5 g, and fry on medium heat, stirring every 30 seconds.
steps.tip: The salt draws water out of the onion so it softens faster and burns less.
steps.visualCue: Onions go soft and clear first, then light golden-brown at the edges, and smell sweet
steps.cameraCheck: The golden onions in the pan
steps.videoShot: Onions turning from white to golden.
steps.watchOut: Dark brown or black edges (bitter curry) or pale raw onion (the gravy tastes sharp); sprinkle a spoon of water and lower the heat if it browns too fast.

steps.title: Add the ginger, garlic and chilli
steps.text: Add the minced ginger, garlic and slit chilli and stir.
steps.visualCue: A sharp, raw garlic smell that turns mellow and golden-toasted
steps.cameraCheck: The pan with the ginger and garlic
steps.videoShot: Ginger and garlic hitting the onions.
steps.watchOut: Garlic browning to dark, which tastes bitter; if it darkens, add the tomato right away.

steps.title: Cook the tomato
steps.text: Add the chopped tomato and cook, stirring and pressing it with the back of the spoon.
steps.visualCue: The tomato breaks down to a thick, jammy paste and a thin film of oil shows at the edge
steps.cameraCheck: The thick tomato paste in the pan
steps.videoShot: Tomato melting into a paste.
steps.watchOut: Stopping too early, when the tomato is still in pieces and smells sour and raw; keep cooking until the oil shows at the edges.

steps.title: Add the powders
steps.text: Add the powder mix and 1 tbsp (15 ml) water, stirring at once.
steps.visualCue: A deep red-brown paste that smells toasty, not harsh
steps.cameraCheck: The masala paste in the pan
steps.videoShot: Powders stirred into the paste with a splash of water.
steps.watchOut: A burnt smell or a dry, sticking paste, which means the pan is too dry; add another splash of water and stir fast.

steps.title: Sear the chicken
steps.text: Add the chicken pieces and stir to coat, then cook on medium-high heat.
steps.visualCue: The outside of the chicken turns white, with no pink on any surface, and the masala clings to the pieces
steps.cameraCheck: The coated chicken in the pan
steps.videoShot: Chicken pieces turning white in the masala.
steps.watchOut: Chicken stewing in water instead of searing, when liquid pools in the pan; raise the heat a little and keep stirring until the liquid reduces.

steps.title: Add the curd
steps.text: Turn the heat to low. Add the whisked curd 1 tbsp at a time, stirring nonstop.
steps.visualCue: The masala turns creamy light-orange and the curd blends in with no white streaks
steps.cameraCheck: The creamy masala in the pan
steps.videoShot: Curd stirred into the masala in small spoonfuls.
steps.watchOut: The curd splitting into tiny white grains and watery liquid, which happens on high heat or if added all at once; take the pan off the heat for 30 seconds, stir well, and go slower. It still tastes fine if it splits, but looks curdled.

steps.title: Simmer covered
steps.text: Add the rest of the salt (about 2.5 g in all for the recipe) and 60 ml (4 tbsp) water, bring to a gentle bubble, cover and cook on low.
steps.visualCue: Small slow bubbles at the edge under the lid, and a savoury spiced smell
steps.cameraCheck: The covered pan, then the gravy once the lid is lifted
steps.videoShot: A lid lifted with steam rising.
steps.watchOut: A dry pan that sticks to the bottom (the curd catches and burns); lift the lid halfway and stir once, and add 2 tbsp water if it looks dry.

steps.title: Check the chicken
steps.text: Cut the biggest piece in half.
steps.visualCue: White all the way through with clear juice, and no pink or rubbery centre; a thermometer reads 75 °C if you use one
steps.videoShot: A chicken piece cut open to show white meat.
steps.watchOut: Pink in the middle, which means it is not safe to eat; cook the pieces 3 more minutes covered and check again.

steps.title: Add the methi leaves
steps.text: Add the chopped leaves and stir them through the gravy.
steps.visualCue: The leaves look like a big green pile that wilts quickly to dark green and a strong, slightly bitter-sweet smell rises
steps.cameraCheck: The pan with the green leaves going in
steps.videoShot: A handful of leaves stirred into the gravy.
steps.watchOut: Adding the leaves too early (the curry goes dark and very bitter) or too late (the leaves taste raw); add them after the chicken is cooked and cook only about 6 more minutes.

steps.title: Cook uncovered
steps.text: Cook on low-medium heat, stirring now and then, until the gravy is thick.
steps.tip: If you are using kasuri methi instead of fresh leaves, crush 1 tbsp between your palms and add it here.
steps.visualCue: The leaves turn dark green and soft, and the gravy thickens until it coats the back of the spoon, with a little oil at the edge
steps.videoShot: The gravy bubbling and thickening.
steps.watchOut: A watery gravy (cook it a few minutes more) or one that is too dry and clumped (add 2 tbsp warm water and stir).

steps.title: Finish with garam masala and lemon
steps.text: Add ½ tsp (1 g) garam masala and ½ tsp (3 ml) lemon juice and stir.
steps.visualCue: A warm, sweet-spicy smell, and the colour lifts slightly with the lemon
steps.cameraCheck: The finished curry in the pan
steps.videoShot: Garam masala sprinkled over the curry.
steps.watchOut: Too much lemon, which can split the curd and sour the gravy; add it a few drops at a time and taste.

steps.title: Rest it
steps.text: Turn off the heat, cover and leave for 2 minutes.
steps.visualCue: The gravy settles and thickens a little, and the oil gathers at the edges
steps.videoShot: A lid placed on the pan.
steps.watchOut: Serving straight away and burning your tongue; the flavours also blend better after resting.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon the curry (about 260 g) into a bowl or plate with roti or rice.
steps.visualCue: Glossy dark-green gravy with white chicken pieces showing through, steaming
steps.videoShot: A slow pan over the bowl with a roti beside it.
steps.watchOut: A thin or pale gravy, which means it needs more cooking; put it back on the heat for 2–3 minutes.

reasons: high protein (about 35 g), good fibre and vitamin C from the fenugreek leaves, no deep frying and modest oil (12 g). Points off for about 1,140 mg sodium and 125 mg cholesterol. Restaurants usually use more oil or butter, cream and more salt, and often skin-on or bone-in pieces.

researchRating.basis: methi chicken (murgh methi) is widely published by Indian recipe blogs and is a well-liked winter curry, with a distinctive flavour; points off because the bitterness divides people (blogs warn to taste the leaves first) and star ratings and comment counts were not visible, as recipe pages could only be seen through search snippets.

storage: Fridge-safe in a clean airtight box for 2–3 days (as stated by two recipe blogs; cool it within 1 hour first). The curry tastes better the next day. Freezer: not stated by the sources seen; chicken curries generally freeze for about 2 months (general guidance), but the leaves darken. Reheat in a pan on low with 2 tbsp water until steaming hot all through, or microwave covered for 2 minutes, stirring once.
leftoverRemix: Methi chicken paratha roll. Shred the cold chicken, mix it with the thick gravy and a little chopped onion, and roll it in a warm roti or paratha as a roll with a squeeze of lemon (FitPlate suggestion, not from a source).
burnOff: about 5.9 km of running (410 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 8.2 km of brisk walking (about 1 h 40 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.).

navratri.reason: chicken, onion and garlic are avoided (most common rule set)

ekadashi.reason: meat, onion and garlic are avoided

jain.reason: chicken, onion, garlic and fresh ginger

ramadan.reason: use halal-sourced chicken; a filling protein dish for sehri, but about 1,140 mg sodium (est.) can add to thirst, so cut the salt to 2 g

jain.reason: chicken, onion, garlic and fresh ginger (root vegetables); Jain rules also exclude meat

glutenFree.reason: no wheat in the recipe and no hing (asafoetida) is used; check the garam masala and chilli powder labels for added flour

dairyFree.reason: curd 40 g is the only dairy; swap for unsweetened coconut yoghurt 40 g (see Dairy-free variant)
